history.period: Present church blessed 1998; origins in the 1980s, with earlier devotion dating to the British tea-estate era
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Roman Catholic Latin Rite Marian pilgrimage shrine near Peermade in Idukki district, dedicated to Our Lady of Good Health (Velankanni Matha), served by the Congregation of the Missionary Brothers of St. Francis (CMSF). Devotion here traces to the British tea-estate era; in the 1980s Bro. Hippolitus Thadathil CMSF, a Franciscan missionary, initiated the present church, an ashram chapel first serving devotees until the new granite church was planned and blessed in 1998. Architect J. P. Bright of Thiruvananthapuram designed it in Gothic Revival style with a large dome (claimed the largest among Christian churches in India), rock-cut portraits at the entrance and a carved-wood altar. It is also known as 'Kochu Velankanni'; two Marian apparition events and miracles are attributed to the shrine, and it was declared a pilgrim centre. Pattumala means 'hill draped in silk'. CSV ERROR FLAG: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name - this church is in KERALA; the actual place is Pattumala near Peermade (CSV town 'Idukki' is the district, ~8 km from Peermade town).

name: Pattumala Matha Church
town_description: Pattumala ('hill draped in silk') is a hill locality near Peermade in Idukki district, Kerala, surrounded by tea plantations. It is a Marian pilgrimage centre known for the granite Gothic church atop the hill, offering views of the Western Ghats.
